summary: The root "mhn" refers to work, labor, or service, including the performance of an office or ministration. It can also denote the clothes worn while performing such duties.
lane: مَِهْنَةٌ ذ [is syn. with عَمَلٌ and فِعْلٌ , and means work, labour, or] service; ministration; performance of an office. (S, &c.) -b2- Also, The clothes worn in service, or in the performance of business. (Msb.)

headwords.def: اِمْتَهَنَهُ He used it for service and work: (K:) i. q. اِبْتَ َلَهُ, q. v.: (S, Msb:) He held it in mean estimation. (Har, p. 65.)

مَِهْنَةٌ [is syn. with عَمَلٌ and فِعْلٌ, and means work, labour, or] service; ministration; performance of an office. (S, &c.) Also, The clothes worn in service, or in the performance of business. (Msb.)
مَهِينٌ Contemptible; abject: (S, K) weak: having little judgment and discrimination. (K.)

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
